# Nehemiah Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 471v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_005_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Now there arose a great outcry of the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers.

**2** Some said, "With our sons and our daughters, we are many. Let us get grain, that we may eat and survive."

**3** Others said, "We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards, and our houses to get grain because of the famine."

**4** Still others said, "We have borrowed money for the king's tax on our fields and vineyards.

**5** Now our flesh is the same as our brothers' flesh, our children are the same as their children. Yet we are forcing our sons and daughters into slavery, and some of our daughters have already been enslaved. We are powerless, for our fields and vineyards belong to others."

**6** I was very angry when I heard their outcry and these words.

**7** I took counsel with myself and brought charges against the nobles and the officials. I said to them, "You are exacting interest, each from his brother!" And I called a great assembly against them.

**8** I said to them, "As far as we were able, we have bought back our Jewish brothers who were sold to the nations. But now you are selling your own brothers, and they are to be sold back to us!" They were silent and could find nothing to say.

**9** So I said, "The thing you are doing is not good. Ought you not to walk in the fear of our God to prevent the reproach of the nations, our enemies?

**10** Moreover, I and my brothers and my servants have been lending them money and grain. Let us abandon this exacting of interest.

**11** Return to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive orchards, and their houses, and the percentage of money, grain, new wine, and oil that you have been exacting from them."

**12** They said, "We will return these things and will require nothing from them. We will do as you say." Then I called the priests and made them swear to do as they had promised.

**13** I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, "So may God shake out every man from his house and from his labor who does not keep this promise. So may he be shaken out and emptied." And all the assembly said "Amen" and praised the LORD. And the people did as they had promised.

**14** Moreover, from the time that I was appointed governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes — twelve years — neither I nor my brothers ate the food allowance of the governor.

**15** The former governors who preceded me laid heavy burdens on the people and took from them food and wine, besides forty shekels of silver. Even their servants lorded it over the people. But I did not do so, because of the fear of God.

**16** I also persevered in the work on this wall, and we acquired no land, and all my servants were gathered there for the work.

**17** Moreover, there were at my table a hundred and fifty Jews and officials, besides those who came to us from the surrounding nations.

**18** Now what was prepared for each day was one ox, six choice sheep, and birds, and every ten days all kinds of wine in abundance. Yet for all this I did not demand the food allowance of the governor, because the service was too heavy on this people.

**19** Remember for my good, O my God, all that I have done for this people.

---

## LOGOS Translation Notes
1. **5:7 "exacting interest"** — Hebrew *mashsha*, referring to loans with interest or usurious lending, which was forbidden between fellow Israelites under Torah law (Exod 22:25; Deut 23:19-20).
2. **5:11 "the percentage"** — Literally "the hundredth," likely indicating a 1% monthly interest rate. The term has been generalized as "percentage" since the exact rate structure is debated.
3. **5:14-18 Nehemiah's self-testimony** — These verses form a distinctive genre within the book: the governor's personal apologia, modeled on ancient Near Eastern royal inscriptions but subordinated to the fear of God rather than royal self-glorification.

*— LOGOS*
